**Yes** are an English [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock) band formed in London in 1968. Having featured [20 full-time musicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Yes_band_members) across their history, their most notable members include lead singer [Jon Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Anderson), bassist [Chris Squire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Squire), guitarists [Steve Howe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Howe) and [Trevor Rabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Rabin), drummers [Bill Bruford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Bruford) and [Alan White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_White_(Yes_drummer)), and keyboardists [Tony Kaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Kaye_(musician)) and [Rick Wakeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Wakeman), who represented Yes when they were inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame) in 2017. Widely regarded as progressive rock pioneers, the group have explored several musical styles and remain one of the most successful, influential, and longest-lasting acts in the genre. [Their discography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes_discography) spans 25 studio albums, with 13.5 million [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America) (RIAA)-certified albums sold in the United States[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes_(band)#cite_note-riaatotal-1) and more than 30 million worldwide.

Founded by Anderson, Squire, Bruford, Kaye, and guitarist [Peter Banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Banks), Yes began performing a mix of original songs and covers spanning rock, pop, blues, and jazz, as showcased on their first two albums, _[Yes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes_(Yes_album))_ (1969) and _[Time and a Word](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_and_a_Word)_ (1970). A change of direction in 1970 following the replacement of Banks with Howe led to a series of celebrated progressive rock albums, including four consecutive US platinum or multi-platinum sellers: _[The Yes Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yes_Album)_ (1971); _[Fragile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fragile_(Yes_album))_ (1971), which included the hit single " [Roundabout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundabout_(Yes_song))"; _[Close to the Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close_to_the_Edge)_ (1972); and the live album _[Yessongs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yessongs)_ (1973). Yes earned a reputation for their elaborate stage sets, light displays, and iconic album covers designed by [Roger Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Dean_(artist)).

In 1983, Squire, White, Anderson, Kaye, and Rabin reformed Yes. This release featured the group's only US number-one single, " [Owner of a Lonely Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owner_of_a_Lonely_Heart)", and won a [Grammy Award for Best Rock Instrumental Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rock_Instrumental_Performance) for the track " [Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_(Yes_song))". Yes continued to tour regularly and release albums—including the symphonically backed _[Magnification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnification_(album))_ (2001)—before entering a temporary hiatus in 2004.

Following the cancellation of a 2008 tour due to Anderson's health, Yes enlisted [Benoît David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beno%C3%AEt_David) as their new lead singer and resumed activity. [Jon Davison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Davison) replaced David in 2012. Three former members toured separately as [Yes Featuring Jon Anderson, Trevor Rabin, Rick Wakeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes_Featuring_Jon_Anderson,_Trevor_Rabin,_Rick_Wakeman) from 2016 to 2018.

# Aurora Tracklisting
When **YES** first began sketching out ideas for what would become ‘ **Aurora**’, the process was loose and exploratory.

Some echo the classic **YES** approach, others push into new territory, but together they form a cohesive whole that honours the band’s heritage while embracing forward motion. With their 24th studio album, **YES** demonstrate not just longevity, but a sustained curiosity, a desire to keep exploring, keep refining and keep discovering their

# Keys To Ascension: The Studio Recordings
The sessions hold a special place in the **YES** story.

This new release includes brand new material from Roger Dean, the artist synonymous with **YES** for many decades, who together with designer Michael Inns have completely refreshed the artwork.

# The Fragile UK Tour 2027
**YES**, are happy to announce new dates for their rescheduled Fragile Tour in May 2027.

The tour will see **YES** performing their 1971 classic album, ‘Fragile’, in its entirety, including such timeless songs as ‘Heart of the Sunrise’, ‘South Side of the Sky’ and the much loved ‘Roundabout’ as well as a selection of songs from right across their illustrious catalogue from their legendary 70`s releases right up to their new studio album ‘Aurora’ out on 12th June.

Each show will feature a gallery of work by esteemed artist, Roger Dean, whose paintings have graced the covers of many of **YES** albums over the years. ‘Fragile’ was the first **YES** album to feature Dean`s iconic artwork.

‘Fragile’ was the fourth album by **YES** cracking the Top 10 in the UK in 1971 achieving Platinum status along the way and was the first to feature keyboardist Rick Wakeman.

# Yes
[IMDbProStarmeter](https://pro.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?rf=cons_nm_meter&ref_=cons_nm_meter) [See rank](https://pro.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?rf=cons_nm_meter&ref_=cons_nm_meter)

![Jon Anderson, Bill Bruford, Steve Howe, Chris Squire, Rick Wakeman, and Yes](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTRlZTBhNTAtMjYzYy00ODYwLTllNDgtYjU5NTJlOWNlMmEwXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UY207_CR11,0,140,207_.jpg)

[Jon Anderson, Bill Bruford, Steve Howe, Chris Squire, Rick Wakeman, and Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/mediaviewer/rm3822409216/?ref_=nm_ov_ph)

[Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) are an English progressive rock band formed in London in 1968 by singer [Jon Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0026963/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and bassist [Chris Squire](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0820085/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). The band has undergone numerous personnel changes throughout its history; twenty musicians have been full-time members. [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) have explored several musical styles over the years, and are most notably regarded as progressive rock pioneers.

The beginnings of [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) can be traced back to Soho, London in April 1968. It was there that singer [Jon Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0026963/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) was introduced to bassist [Chris Squire](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0820085/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) by [Jack Barrie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2911291/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) at La Chasse Club on Wardour Street, a few doors down from the legendary Marquee Club. On 18 May 1968, [Jon Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0026963/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) joined [Mabel Greer's Toyshop](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9864588/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) on stage during the encore of a London gig, performing "Midnight Hour" alongside [Chris Squire](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0820085/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), singer/guitarist [Clive Bayley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9700688/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), guitarist [Peter Banks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2593108/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and drummer [Robert Hagger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9733122/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). The group had been formed by [Clive Bayley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9700688/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Robert Hagger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9733122/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in summer 1967, [Chris Squire](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0820085/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Peter Banks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2593108/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) having joined in the winter following the break up of [The Syn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9864587/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).

Anderson, Bayley and Squire put an advertisement in the Melody Maker music magazine, which led to the recruitment of drummer [Bill Bruford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0115756/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He rehearsed with the group in the basement of the Lucky Horseshoe Café on Shaftesbury Avenue on 7 June and then played his first gig with them that evening.

During this time, they recruited [Tony Kaye](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0443412/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as organist, making [Mabel Greer's Toyshop](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9864588/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) a quintet. They played a single gig in July 1968, in Kingston, Surrey on the 20th, followed by an after-party at Bayley's parents' house nearby. Very soon after the gig, [Clive Bayley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9700688/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) left [Mabel Greer's Toyshop](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9864588/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), the group he had formed. [Peter Banks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2593108/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) re-joined as guitarist in late July.

After a few more rehearsals in the basement of the Lucky Horseshoe, the group emerged on 3 August with a new name, [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) (suggested by Banks), and played their first gig, that evening, in Essex. Well rehearsed and different, [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) began growing support around London. Wallace had previously played alongside Anderson in [The Warriors](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2741669/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). The group played a gig at Leeds University, with O'Reilly back on drums, which Buford attended with friends to show them the group he used to play in.

By the spring, they had secured a record deal with Atlantic Records and began recording their debut album, "Yes", which opened with the [Mabel Greer's Toyshop](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9864588/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) track "Beyond and Before".

In early May 1970, with new guitarist [Steve Howe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0397895/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), the group moved to Devon to write their third album. In September, the group filmed the television special [Rock of the 70s: Yes (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2586086/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) with Howe miming to Banks' parts. "The Yes Album" was recorded in London in late 1970 and released in January 1971. With new manager [Brian Lane](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0485254/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) finally began finding success. "The Yes Album" made it into the UK charts and they made their USA debut tour in summer 1971. The group performed "Yours Is No Disgrace" on [Episode #8.13 (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1157393/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Episode #1.66 (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0520453/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).

With new keyboard-player [Rick Wakeman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0906857/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), the group began rehearsing their fourth album, "Fragile", in August 1971. Released in autumn, it became their first big hit record in the UK and "Roundabout" became their first big hit single in the USA. An October show was filmed for the television program [Yes (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0984119/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). 1972 saw the group produce their fifth album: "Close to the Edge", which was followed by Bruford's second departure from the band, leaving this time to join [King Crimson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1072743/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). His replacement, drummer [Alan White](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0924425/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), joined just a few days before a big American tour.

Shows from the autumn 1972 "Close to the Edge" tour were recorded and released on the successful "Yessongs" album the following year. A December London show was recorded for the concert film [Yessongs (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070940/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). 1973 also saw the group release their sixth studio album: "Tales from Topographic Oceans". He was replaced by Swiss [Patrick Moraz](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0603221/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) for the "Relayer" album, recorded in 1974 and followed by extensive touring into 1975.

In autumn, the group headed to Montreux, Switzerland to work on their eighth studio album. After a short time, Moraz parted ways and [Rick Wakeman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0906857/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) was brought back. The group made their first music video for "Wonderous Stories", which was aired on [Episode #14.40 (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0730404/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).

Rehearsing as a trio, Squire, Howe and White recruited singer [Trevor Horn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0394924/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and keyboard-player [Geoff Downes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1168919/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), who had just had a big hit as [The Buggles](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1477902/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) with "Video Killed the Radio Star". Horn and Downes made the second Buggles album, while Howe began working with [John Wetton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1226101/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).

After that fell through, the duo made the Christmas single "Run with the Fox". In January 1982, they formed a new group, Cinema, with guitar/singer [Trevor Rabin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0704909/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Original [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) keyboard-player [Tony Kaye](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0443412/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) was brought in and work began on an album, with [Trevor Horn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0394924/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) back this time as producer rather than a band member. With Anderson joining the group, making them from a quartet to a quintet, plans to name themselves Bunch of Daffs were aborted when they realized they were [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) again, with three original members.

The album featured the hit single "Owner of a Lonely Heart", which made it to number one in the USA chart. The [Yes: Owner of a Lonely Heart (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8184970/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) music video features [Eddie Jobson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0423423/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) on keyboards. After the album's completion, [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) parted ways from the group. Kaye appears in the [Yes: Leave It (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8432022/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) music video.

The [Yes: 9012 Live (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0204116/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) concert film was shot at Edmonton, Canada in September 1984.

By spring 1991, Squire, Rabin, White and Kaye had joined forced with ABWH to form an eight-man [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) line-up. They released the studio album "Union" and embarked on a world tour, finishing in spring 1992. One by one, Bruford, Howe and Wakeman left the group, reverting back to the "90125" line-up.

Russian keyboard-player [Igor Khoroshev](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1030505/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) was recruited for the autumn 1997 tour.

An October 1999 show was filmed for the [House of Yes: Live from House of Blues (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0311302/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) concert film. Rather than recruiting another keyboard player, Anderson, Squire, Howe and White made the "Magnification" album with an orchestra and White handling piano parts. On tour, [Tom Brislin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1967228/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) was brought in as keyboard player. The concert film [Yes: Symphonic Live (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0468586/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) was filmed in Amsterdam in November 2001.

During those two years, numerous DVDs were made: [Yesspeak (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0391540/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Yes Acoustic (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0996545/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Songs from Tsongas: Yes 35th Anniversary Concert (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1006959/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Yes: Live at Montreux 2003 (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0996546/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). After a November 2004 London gig with the line-up of Squire, Howe, White, Downes and Rabin, the group went on hiatus for three years, during which time Howe rejoined [Asia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2902745/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) alongside Downes and Squire re-formed [The Syn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9864587/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) with White. Wakeman had suggested his eldest son [Oliver Wakeman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3029465/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as keyboard-player.

Tired of waiting for Anderson, the trio of Howe, Squire and White, along with [Oliver Wakeman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3029465/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and new singer [Benoît David](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3198796/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) began touring America in autumn 2008. The "In the Present" touring cycle continued to spring 2011, recording a live album in France in December 2009, which was released two years later along with an accompanying DVD documentary: [Yes: In the Present - Live from Lyon (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2803728/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). This line-up had entered the studio with [Trevor Horn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0394924/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in autumn 2010 and worked on a "Drama"-era song called "Fly from Here".

The Davison, Squire, Howe, White, Downes line-up entered the studio in 2014 to make the "Heaven and Earth" album. Throughout 2014 and 2015, the group played four 1970s albums in their entirety live on tour, releasing two live concert album-video sets: [Like It Is: Yes at the Bristol Hippodrome (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3674494/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) (featuring "Going for the One" and "The Yes Album") and [Like It Is: Yes at Mesa Arts Centre (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3907446/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) (featuring "Close to the Edge" and "Fragile"). Whilst ill, Squire had suggested multi-instrumentalist and former [Yes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2898703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) member [Billy Sherwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2457453/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as his replacement. This line-up continuing playing original albums in their entirety with "Drama" and "Tales from Topographic Oceans". Both Schellen and White appear on 2017's "Topographic Drama" live album. A six-man line-up toured America in summer 2017, with Howe's eldest son [Dylan Howe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2600259/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) drumming alongside White to create a richer drum sound whilst White continued to recover from back surgery.

Squire was represented by widow [Scotland Squire](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm10304699/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and their daughter Xilan. The other six members attended, all except for Bruford performed live together.

The line-up of Davison, Sherwood, Howe, White and Downes celebrated the group's fiftieth anniversary in 2018 with original keyboard-player [Tony Kaye](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0443412/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as special guest and [Jay Schellen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2941050/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) sharing drumming duties to White not being fully recovered. During the world tour, former members [Bill Bruford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0115756/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Patrick Moraz](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0603221/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Trevor Horn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0394924/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Tom Brislin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1967228/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) all reunited with the group on stage, all performed except Bruford; having retired as a musician some years before, he introduced the group at their London Palladium concert. Concert footage and interviews were filmed during the fiftieth anniversary tour for the documentary [Yes 50: Yesterday, Today, Tomorrow (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt9503616/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).

results.description:
**Yes**

Founded in 1968, Yes proved to be one of the longest lasting and the most successful of the 1970s' Progressive Rock groups. The name Yes was chosen for the band as something short, direct, and memorable.

Their debut single, entitled "Sweetness", was released soon after and their first album, "Yes" was issued in November of 1969.

Two months later, Trevor Horn (vocals, guitar) and Geoff Downes (keyboards), formerly of the British band, Buggles, joined the Yes line-up of Steve Howe, Chris Squire, and Alan White.

In late 1983, this Yes line-up, with guitarist/vocalist Trevor Horn serving as producer, released an unexpected chart-topping hit single (number one in the U.S. in January of 1984) in "Owner Of A Lonely Heart", displaying a stripped-down, modern Dance/Rock sound unlike anything the group had ever produced before. Yes was fairly inactive for nearly two years after that until the late 1987 release of "The Big Generator", which performed only moderately well.

With their success re-kindled, the four sued the other various members who had toured as Yes over the legal use of the name.

After a South American tour in 2010, Yes embarked on a North American tour called Rite of Spring, which concluded with two shows in Mexico in May 2011.

Yes was slated to return to New Zealand and Australia for an April, 2012 tour that would also include stops in Japan, Indonesia and Hawaii. In mid-March, 2014, Yes hit the road again, kicking off what they called their Three Album Tour in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. Much to the delight of their fans, Yes was slated to be inducted into Cleveland's Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame on April 17, 2017.

In April, 2018, to honor the 50th anniversary of their debut album, Anderson, Rabin and Wakeman announced a tour they called Quintessential Yes: The 50th Anniversary Tour, set to kick off in Europe in June. A September 7 release date was set for "Yes: 50th Anniversary Live At The Apollo" on DVD, Blu-ray, 2 CD and 3 LP. Meanwhile, another version of Yes, currently run by longtime guitarist Steve Howe and drummer Alan White, was scheduled to tour America with singer Jon Davison.

The trek would feature classic Yes songs as well as selections from a new solo album called "1000 Hands". Early September brought the news that Yes planned an October 30th release for "The Royal Affair Tour: Live From Las Vegas", a live album recorded July 26th, 2019 at the Hard Rock Hotel in Las Vegas.

In the other camp, Steve Howe posted a notice on the band's website that a new Yes album titled "The Quest" would be released August 1st, 2021.

Yes planned to celebrate the 50th anniversary of "Close to the Edge" with a 2022 Fall tour of the U.S., marking their first stateside outing since 2019.

Yes co-founder Jon Anderson was still busy in 2025 with a tour of the United States, while band members, guitarist Steve Howe, keyboardist Geoff Downes, singer Jon Davison, bassist Billy Sherwood and drummer Jay Schellen were booked for twenty-nine shows in October and November.
